basis: The archive is content input, not an instruction source. Its renderer was not executed and its embedded placement/verification claims were independently reviewed. All 29 mnemonics are added as accessible text in an eight-category library. Contradictory illustrations are archived outside the deployment instead of silently displaying uncorrected teaching. Existing notes, question banks, posters, seven memory-sheet mnemonics and page layouts remain intact; an additive route extension supplies compact related links. The seven existing memory-sheet aids are indexed by title/category only and always link to the unchanged original sheet.

edits.reason: Correct attribution and distinguish emergency action from prompt contact; remove the unsupported claim that fainting and seizures are interchangeable. Include the current AWHONN low-temperature warning too.

items.v: Thoughts of harming self or baby

original.note: The ACOG standard. The site notes list fainting where ACOG has seizures; same red-flag family. Any one of these means urgent assessment, do not wait for the scheduled visit.
original.title: POST-BIRTH

items.v: Thoughts of harming self or baby

reviewed.note: AWHONN’s POST-BIRTH warning signs: chest pain, breathing difficulty, seizures or thoughts of harm need emergency help. Other listed signs need prompt clinical contact; if care cannot be reached, seek emergency care. Fainting is also concerning and is not interchangeable with seizures. Tell the team when you gave birth.

edits.reason: Limit the side-lying examination advice to perineal inspection, rather than every surgical incision.

original.note: Assess the repair or incision in side-lying or Sims position. Worsening redness, drainage, or separation is a flag, not expected recovery.
original.title: REEDA

reviewed.note: Assess redness, swelling, bruising, drainage and wound-edge approximation. Side-lying/Sims can help perineal inspection; assess a cesarean incision in an appropriate comfortable position. Worsening redness, drainage, separation or fever needs review.

edits.reason: Replace a prevention guarantee and clarify that “alone” does not mean a separate room.

items.v: Alone: baby sleeps alone, no bed-sharing
Back: on the back for every sleep
Crib: firm flat surface, empty crib, nothing loose

original.note: No blankets, pillows, or toys in the sleep space. Every sleep, every time, including naps.
original.title: ABCs of Safe Sleep

reviewed.hook: Three letters for safer infant sleep

items.v: Alone on a separate infant sleep surface; share a room, not a bed.
Back: on the back for every sleep
Crib: firm flat surface, empty crib, nothing loose

reviewed.note: Back for every sleep on a firm, flat, level surface with no loose bedding, pillows or toys. Room-share without bed-sharing, ideally for at least the first six months. These measures reduce risk; they do not guarantee prevention of SIDS.

edits.reason: Surfactant may be deficient rather than wholly absent; distinguish exposure from aspiration and preserve current suction safety.

original.hook: Three causes of newborn breathing trouble

items.v: Respiratory distress syndrome: no surfactant, stiff lungs, mostly preterm.
Transient tachypnea: lung fluid not cleared, often term or late preterm, often after cesarean without labor. Improves over days.
Meconium aspiration: meconium breathed in, blocks and inflames airways, often postterm or meconium-stained fluid.

original.note: Signs overlap, so use birth history and the exam together. RDS is a surfactant problem, TTN is a fluid problem, MAS is a blockage problem.
original.title: RDS, TTN, MAS

reviewed.hook: Three causes of newborn breathing trouble

items.v: Respiratory distress syndrome: insufficient surfactant promotes alveolar collapse, especially in preterm infants.
Transient tachypnea: lung fluid not cleared, often term or late preterm, often after cesarean without labor. Improves over days.
Meconium aspiration: meconium breathed in, blocks and inflames airways, often postterm or meconium-stained fluid.

reviewed.note: RDS is primarily a surfactant problem; TTN is delayed fluid clearance; MAS involves aspiration with obstruction/inflammation. Signs overlap, so assess history and condition. Meconium-stained fluid alone does not diagnose aspiration or justify routine suctioning.

edits.reason: Correct the foramen-ovale function, partial liver bypass and misleading claim that each shunt skips a separate organ in serial order.

original.hook: Three fetal shunts, in blood-flow order

items.v: Ductus venosus bypasses the liver, sending umbilical blood toward the inferior vena cava.
Foramen ovale bypasses the right-to-left heart circuit, right atrium to left atrium.
Ductus arteriosus bypasses the lungs, pulmonary artery to descending aorta.

original.note: Each shunt skips one organ. The cord rule: 1 vein in (oxygen-rich), 2 arteries out (oxygen-poor).
original.title: Liver, Heart, Lungs

reviewed.hook: Three fetal shunts and the pathways they bypass

items.v: Ductus venosus directs some umbilical venous blood toward the inferior vena cava, bypassing much of the liver.
Foramen ovale allows right atrium → left atrium flow, bypassing much of the lung circulation.
Ductus arteriosus connects pulmonary artery → descending aorta, bypassing much of the lung circulation.

reviewed.note: These are branching pathways, not a single stream passing through all three shunts. One umbilical vein brings relatively oxygen-rich blood toward the fetus; two umbilical arteries return blood toward the placenta.

edits.reason: State the fresh-milk scope and distinguish thawed/leftover clocks without changing the supplied illustration.

items.v: At room temperature, up to 77 F (25 C)
Freezer best, up to 12 months acceptable, at 0 F (-18 C)

original.note: Never microwave milk and never refreeze fully thawed milk. Thaw in the refrigerator or lukewarm water.

items.v: At room temperature, up to 77 F (25 C)
Freezer best, up to 12 months acceptable, at 0 F (-18 C)

reviewed.note: Never microwave milk and never refreeze fully thawed milk. Thaw in the refrigerator or lukewarm water. Once fully thawed in the refrigerator, use within 24 hours; use within two hours after warming or bringing to room temperature. Use milk left after a feed within two hours.
reviewed.context: For freshly expressed milk for a healthy term infant at home. Hospital/preterm instructions may differ.

edits.reason: Make clear that the age criterion concerns the infant.

items.v: All breastmilk: full or nearly full breastfeeding

original.note: Feeding gaps no longer than 4 hours by day, 6 by night. All three must hold. One fails, LAM fails.
original.title: LAM and the 3 A's

items.v: Age: the infant is younger than six months.
All breastmilk: full or nearly full breastfeeding

reviewed.note: Feeding gaps no longer than 4 hours by day, 6 by night. All three must hold. One fails, LAM fails.
reviewed.context: All three criteria must remain true, including feeding gaps no longer than four hours by day and six hours by night.

edits.reason: Qualify classic patterns; avoid diagnosing from pain or blood color alone.

items.v: Painless, bright-red bleeding, soft nontender uterus. Placenta covers the cervical opening.
Painful, dark-red bleeding, rigid tender uterus. Placenta separates early; blood can hide behind it.

original.note: No digital vaginal exam before previa is excluded. In abruption, visible bleeding can underestimate severity, and DIC is a risk.
original.title: Painless Previa, Painful Abruption

items.v: Classically painless bright-red bleeding with a soft uterus; placenta covers the cervical opening.
Often pain, uterine tenderness/firmness and possible bleeding; placenta separates early and blood may be concealed.

reviewed.note: Patterns overlap: pain, blood color or visible amount cannot establish or exclude either diagnosis. No digital vaginal examination before previa is excluded. Assess maternal perfusion and fetal status urgently; abruption can cause shock or DIC.

edits.reason: Complete the immediate toxicity response beyond “reach for” the antidote; retain individual hold parameters.

original.hook: Check before you give it and while it runs
original.note: Toxicity signs: respirations under 12 per minute, urine output under 25 to 30 mL per hour, absent or decreasing reflexes. If any R fails, stop the drip and reach for calcium gluconate.
original.title: Magnesium and the 3 R's

reviewed.hook: Check before you give it and while it runs
reviewed.note: Absent/decreasing reflexes, respiratory depression or oliguria are concerning; common escalation values include respirations <12/min or urine <25–30 mL/hour, with local hold parameters. For suspected toxicity: stop magnesium, call the emergency/obstetric team, support breathing and prepare prescribed calcium gluconate. Do not wait for a laboratory result or give an antidote without the actual order/protocol.

edits.reason: Separate hypertension from preeclampsia diagnosis and make OR boundaries explicit.

original.hook: Two blood pressure lines in preeclampsia

items.v: Preeclampsia starts here: systolic 140 or diastolic 90 or higher, on repeat measures.
Severe: confirm within about 15 minutes, treat within 30 to 60 minutes.

original.note: Severe features: Head (persistent severe headache), Eyes (visual change), Belly (right-upper-quadrant or epigastric pain). Labs: platelets under 100,000, creatinine over 1.1. Preeclampsia does not require proteinuria.
original.title: 140/90 Is the Door, 160/110 Is the Alarm

reviewed.hook: Two blood pressure lines in preeclampsia

items.v: Hypertension threshold: systolic ≥140 OR diastolic ≥90 mm Hg on appropriate repeat measurements.
Severe-range BP: systolic ≥160 OR diastolic ≥110 mm Hg needs immediate escalation, prompt confirmation and timely prescribed treatment.

reviewed.note: BP alone does not diagnose preeclampsia. New hypertension after 20 weeks plus proteinuria OR qualifying organ dysfunction supports the diagnosis; chronic hypertension can have superimposed disease. Persistent severe BP is commonly confirmed within about 15 minutes and treated within 30–60 minutes of confirmation; do not wait hours or for proteinuria.

edits.reason: Qualify the indication for CMV testing and specify genital lesions/prodrome at labor, rather than any HSV lesion.

original.hook: Infections that can reach the fetus

items.v: Toxoplasmosis: cook meat, wash produce, let someone else handle cat litter.
Other, syphilis in these notes: transplacental infection, treat with penicillin.
Rubella: early infection can cause heart, eye, and hearing problems. MMR before pregnancy or postpartum, never during.
CMV: can cause hearing loss and growth or neurologic problems. Test by saliva or urine PCR in the first 21 days.
Herpes simplex: most neonatal infection happens during birth. Active lesions usually mean cesarean.

original.note: TORCH is a reminder of possible congenital and perinatal infections, not a diagnosis by itself.
original.title: TORCH

reviewed.hook: Infections that can reach the fetus

items.v: Toxoplasmosis: cook meat, wash produce, let someone else handle cat litter.
Other, syphilis in these notes: transplacental infection, treat with penicillin.
Rubella: early infection can cause heart, eye, and hearing problems. MMR before pregnancy or postpartum, never during.
CMV: congenital infection can affect hearing, growth or neurologic development. When suspected, collect appropriate saliva/urine testing within 21 days.
Herpes simplex: most neonatal infection is acquired during birth. Genital lesions or prodrome at labor generally indicate cesarean birth.

reviewed.note: TORCH is a reminder of possible congenital and perinatal infections, not a diagnosis by itself.

edits.reason: Make the units and diagnostic-test distinction visible.

original.note: 100-gram, 3-hour test. At or above a threshold is abnormal; at least two of the four values are needed for a GDM diagnosis. Screen first with the 50-gram, 1-hour challenge at 24 to 28 weeks.

reviewed.note: 100-gram, 3-hour test. At or above a threshold is abnormal; at least two of the four values are needed for a GDM diagnosis. Screen first with the 50-gram, 1-hour challenge at 24 to 28 weeks.
reviewed.context: All four thresholds are in mg/dL. These are diagnostic 100-g test values, not glucose treatment targets or the 50-g screen cutoffs.

edits.reason: Correct the supplied H-E-L-L-E-R-R spelling to HELPERR and remove the claim that every step is a compulsory sequence.

items.v: Help: call for help, start timing from birth of the head
Legs: McRoberts, thighs sharply flexed toward the abdomen
Lift: suprapubic pressure just above the pubic bone
Enter: internal rotation, the Woods screw
Roll to all-fours, the Gaskin maneuver

original.note: Never fundal pressure, never forceful jerking or downward traction on the head. The site notes cover Help, Legs, Pressure, and Enter; the full HELPERR sequence is the clinical standard.
original.title: HELPERR

items.v: Help: call for help, start timing from birth of the head
Legs: McRoberts, thighs sharply flexed toward the abdomen
Pressure: directed suprapubic pressure above the pubic bone.
Enter: internal rotation, the Woods screw
Roll to all-fours, the Gaskin maneuver

reviewed.note: A team memory aid, not a mandatory order or a bedside training protocol. Call for help immediately and assist within training. Episiotomy may create room for internal maneuvers but does not relieve the bony obstruction. Internal rotation, posterior-arm delivery and all-fours positioning are clinician-directed options. Never fundal pressure or forceful head/neck traction.

original.hook: Four cues of suspected intraamniotic infection
original.note: Suspected intraamniotic infection means recognize and escalate. Mother and baby both need assessment and the team needs to know.
original.title: Fever, Fast Heart, Tender Uterus, Foul Fluid

reviewed.hook: Four cues of suspected intraamniotic infection
reviewed.note: Suspected intraamniotic infection means recognize and escalate. Mother and baby both need assessment and the team needs to know.
reviewed.context: Recognition cues, not a checklist requiring all four findings. Escalate a concerning pattern promptly; the clinical team determines diagnosis and treatment.
